subject: Post-demo: Deployment isolation pathways & ops checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medintegrate.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Deployment isolation pathways & ops checklist

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Short recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary from our call
- Primary constraint: you mentioned PHI workloads and a regulatory requirement to ensure no co-mingling with other customers.
- Secondary: you want audit evidence for data access and the ability to use your own KMS/HSM for key custody.
- Timing: procurement window targeting end of Q4, pilot for a single model in November.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
1) Do you require network-level segregation (customer-managed VPC peering / private link) and a separate control plane, or would single-tenant compute (dedicated GPU pools) with strict tenancy be sufficient?
2) Is BYOK mandatory from day one, or would a staged approach (Redwood-hosted keys initially, BYOK for production) work?
3) Will MedIntegrate perform external audits and need full audit log exports (S3 or secure share)?
4) Are there any egress restrictions for model artifacts or logs leaving your network?

Proposed next steps
- I attached a short SOC2 summary and a blank deployment matrix (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, deployment-matrix.xlsx) to capture where you land on each control.
- If you confirm network + BYOK as must-haves, recommend we schedule a technical workshop with Neha (infra lead) and your network/security engineer to walk VPC connectivity and HSM options.
- Tentative workshop slots: Oct 20 (10:00–11:30 PT) or Oct 22 (08:00–09:30 PT). Which works for your team?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); deployment-matrix.xlsx (Excel, blank template)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medintegrate.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@medintegrate.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Deployment isolation pathways & ops checklist

Jordan — thanks, quick answers inline:

1) Network + control plane isolation is required. We cannot have any multi-tenant control plane access that could potentially reference PHI or tenant identifiers.
2) BYOK is preferred for production; pilot can use Redwood-managed keys if needed but must have a clear migration path.
3) Yes — we perform annual SOC2+HIPAA readiness checks and will need audit log exports (immutable where possible).
4) No broad egress allowed. Logs/artifacts must be exported to our S3 bucket in our account or accessed via secure share.

We are seriously considering Private VPC (or on-prem if connectivity constraints force it). Please include HSM integration options and any lead times for dedicated hardware or HSM procurement in your proposal. Also, procurement will want a high-level bill-of-materials (cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Priya (copied) will coordinate availability for the technical workshop. Tentatively prefer Oct 22.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering | MedIntegrate
sanjay@medintegrate.com | +1 (312) 555-0168

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medintegrate.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Deployment isolation pathways & ops checklist

Thanks Sanjay — this is helpful and aligns with what we expected. Short response + concrete next steps below.

Quick differences and what we'll propose
- Hosted API: fastest to start, no control-plane isolation, Redwood-managed keys, shared control plane — NOT recommended for PHI.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): single-tenant compute (no other customer VMs on the same GPUs) but control plane and orchestration still hosted by Redwood. Good for strong compute isolation with simpler ops, supports audit logs and BYOK.
- Private VPC / On-prem: customer VPC peering or private link + optional customer-managed control plane. Enables full network isolation, customer KMS/HSM, and direct audit exports to your S3. Higher ops and lead time; best match for strict PHI/regulatory constraints.

HSM and BYOK
- We support external KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) with key import (BYOK) for encryption at rest and signing. HSM-backed key material (Cloud HSM / Custody HSM) is supported for production deployments — we'll need to align on vendor and provisioning window.

Attachments and artifacts
- I uploaded a VPC connection guide and an updated deployment matrix with our recommended default for a PHI pilot (vpc-connection-guide.pdf, deployment-matrix.xlsx). See the matrix for a side-by-side cost/ops/latency comparison.

Proposed next actions
1) Technical workshop (Neha + our infra lead + your network/security + Priya) — propose Oct 22, 09:00–10:30 PT. Please confirm attendee list.
2) Redwood to produce a draft BOM and procurement lead times for Dedicated vs Private (we'll include HSM options). Expect a 3–5 business day turnaround after the workshop.
3) During the workshop we'll also capture the exact audit log retention/format requirements so we can provide a sample export.

If Oct 22 works I’ll schedule and include a short pre-read (one-pager) that summarizes the recommended pilot architecture.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: vpc-connection-guide.pdf (PDF, 4 pages); deployment-matrix.xlsx (Excel, populated)
